newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf security a regional responsibility - Velayati.
newsitem.headline: Gulf security a regional responsibility - Velayati.

text.p: Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Sunday that security in the oil-rich Gulf region is the responsibility of Gulf states.
"We have always said that the security of this region should be in the hands of its own people," Velayati told a news conference in the Saudi capital Riyadh.
"Prince Sultan (Saudi Arabia's defence minister) had voiced the same demand lately," Velayti added.

Riyadh and Tehran are at odds over the presence of U.S. and other Western forces in the Gulf. Iran is critical of the Western presence, including about 5,000 U.S. forces in Saudi Arabia, which it says contributes to regional tension.
Asked about an unannounced non-aggression accord among Gulf states, he said:" I am not aware where such an accord or treaty had been prepared. This did not happen at the foreign ministry."
"Let me assure you that there is concurrence among us as to arrangements for stability and arriving at security measures in the region," he said.
Saudi Arabia and its Gulf Arab allies have accused non-Arab Iran of interfering in their internal affairs, which Iran denies, and voice concern over Iran's arms build-up.

Relations between radical Shi'ite Iran and Sunni-ruled Saudi Arabia are bracing for a period of heightened tension over the annual haj pilgrimage to the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. This year's haj falls in mid-April.
Iran insists that its pilgrims hold political rallies to denounce Israel and the United Staes during haj. Saudi Arabia insists that haj, one of the five pillars of Islam should not be politicised.
Iranian media have called Velayati's visit highly significant and said it was likely to help ease tension in the strategic Gulf region.

Velayati, who arrived in Riyadh on Saturday on his first visit to the kingdom since 1993, held talks with his Saudi counterpart Prince Saud al-Faisal and extended an invitation to the Saudi monarch King Fahd to attend an Islamic summit in Tehran in December.
Diplomatic sources said Velayati flew to Medina and is expected to return to Riyadh later in the day for talks with the Saudi Crown Prince Abdullah.
